original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: For the selected P112 pairing model, do two distinct orthogonal 8-frames that share one binary direction r have correction blocks in one common rational rank-8 row space, with a low-rank coefficient interface over F2?
scope_change_reason: The claimed #2278 single-frame probe priced the correction at 16 additively or 8 under matrix coefficients, both at the boundary of the one-frame gate. The distinct experiment pairs frames with common r and tests whether one correction basis can serve both, rather than optimizing a single frame or the incumbent exact 8-term decoder.
mathematical_object: The 112 selected q labels in complex-nine-native DATA-PHASES.json, mapped by their full binary pairing and deleted-frame signature to P112 in the pinned E8 line model. For each common r and frame S, M(S,r) is the 8 by 112 integer Gram correction supported on T={b in P112\S: beta(r,b)=0 and some a in S has odd inner product with b}.
changed_assumption_or_expense: Two distinct frame upgrades may share one rank-8 rational correction basis, with coefficient transformations priced jointly over F2, instead of charging the two frame corrections independently. Interface access, copying, frame transitions and restoration remain unpriced until a supplier is assembled.
method: Exact E8 Gram and F2 arithmetic; enumerate all 1260 orthogonal frames in selected P112 and every r in F2^8 satisfying beta(r,a)=1 on the frame. For each same-r family, choose a full-rank 8-column minor from one correction block and compute exact coefficients for every other block; check reconstruction entrywise, rational rank, integrality and coefficient rank over F2.
domain_and_stop_rule: Finite exhaustive domain: all 1260 selected P112 frames, all valid r values (16 per frame), all 135 distinct directions and 1,539,720 unordered same-r frame pairs. Stop after the exact factorization census and one pinned favorable moment screen; do not claim supplier or kappa without interface and restoration charges.
predecessors_and_overlap: Discussion #2278, philippeVV: single-frame plane-upgrade probe and request to test whether corrections can be absorbed; this work changes the object to pairs of frames sharing r.
PR #1825: paired plane-port decoder (related plane interface, no same-r shared correction census).
Discussion #2126: scalar identity fit over 56 shared matched planes (different fitting object).
Discussion #2024 / PR #2041: selected-P112 tri-plane factorization (different multi-plane decomposition).
Discussion #2292: five-dimensional port decoder (different cover and correction structure).
Discussion #2245 / PR #2251: P104 pooled correction-space dimension 96 (different trace, target matrices and question; noted as current related work).
bottleneck_link: The correction charge was the limiting local price for plane upgrades. Sharing one rational correction basis across two frames could halve that charge and move the selected-word 5% moment screen from above one to below one, provided all other interface costs can be admitted.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json records the 112-label isomorphism and a witness pair. verify.py exhaustively checks the 1,539,720 same-r pairs through 20,160 correction blocks, exact common rational row spaces, integral coefficient maps, F2 ranks, mutation controls, and exact-rational moment controls.
author: Cinna Davis with OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for literature/overlap search, exact-model implementation, code, arithmetic checks, packaging and documentation. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the shared correction basis and its F2 coefficient interface be realized while both source and target frames are available in the actual nine-stage supplier?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The local moment screen has only a finite margin; extra access, copies, hosting, transitions, precision and restoration charges may erase it.
open_questions.first_step: Place the two witness frames into a concrete selected-word schedule and write the complete read/write and restoration ledger before synthesizing a larger word.
open_questions.blocked_by: No chronological host schedule or physical source/target representation for these exact correction factors has been constructed.

open_questions.question: Does the joint correction charge stay at 8 after the exact factors are embedded in the producer's coefficient convention?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact factorization proves a common rational row space, while the +8 moment charge assumes the rank-8/rank-4 coefficient pricing from the local model.

stop_rule: Enumerate the full finite domain once, complete exact reconstruction and negative controls, run the favorable moment gate, and stop without claiming a supplier if any required hosting/interface/restoration term is missing.
